extracted.intended_audience: Users of PARI/GP performing algebraic number theory computations (computational number theorists, mathematicians writing scripts using nf/bnf/bnr functions).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using PARI/GP number field and class-field routines (nfinit, bnfinit, bnrinit, and related bnf*/bnr* functions): how to format inputs, interpret outputs, important flags/limitations, and correctness considerations (notably GRH-dependence and certification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative matrix is an m × n matrix whose entries are elements of K, in any form; its m columns Aj represent elements in K^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns are treated as elements of K^n; entries can be given in any acceptable PARI/GP form (polmods, algebraic numbers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal list
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal list is a row vector of fractional ideals of the number field nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used together with relative matrices to describe ZK-modules (see pseudo-matrix). Ideal lists encode the fractional-ideal scalars associated to columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: A pseudo-matrix is a 2-component row vector (A, I) where A is a relative m × n matrix and I an ideal list of length n; if I = {a1,...,an} and columns are (A1,...,An), this data defines the torsion-free (projective) ZK-module a1 A1 ⊕ ... ⊕ an An.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pseudo-matrices to represent projective ZK-modules inside K^m; many rnf routines return ZK-modules via pseudo-bases (A,I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral pseudo-matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: An integral pseudo-matrix is a 3-component row vector w(A, I, J) where A = (ai,j) is an m × n relative matrix and I = (b1,...,bm), J = (a1,...,an) are ideal lists such that ai,j ∈ b_i a_j^{-1} for all i,j; it defines projective modules N,P and a ZK-linear map f : N → P, and M = P / f(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integral pseudo-matrices to represent arbitrary ZK-modules of finite type in K^m, including torsion; the containment condition ai,j ∈ b_i a_j^{-1} ensures integrality of the matrix entries relative to the ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective ZK-modules via pseudo-matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Any projective ZK-module of finite type in K^m can be given by a pseudo-matrix (A,I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing modules that are projective and torsion-free, provide a pseudo-basis (A,I) with appropriate K-linear independence conditions on the columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral pseudo-matrix represents arbitrary ZK-modules with torsion
rubrics_metrics.description: An arbitrary ZK-module of finite type in K^m, with non-trivial torsion, is given by an integral pseudo-matrix (A,I,J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To include torsion information, use the 3-component integral pseudo-matrix form; this encodes both the free/projective and torsion structure via the ideals I,J and matrix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-basis condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The pair (A,I) is a pseudo-basis of the module it generates if the aj are non-zero and the Aj are K-linearly independent (size n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a relative matrix A this means A must be square with non-zero determinant. When in Hermite Normal Form (HNF) it is upper triangular and all diagonal elements equal 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermite Normal Form (HNF) for relative matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative matrix A is in Hermite Normal Form if it is upper triangular and all elements of the diagonal are equal to 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HNF is the canonical triangular form used for pseudo-bases; PARI/GP routines often return or expect HNF when treating pseudo-bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant of a pseudo-basis / pseudo-matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: The determinant of a pseudo-basis (A,I) is the ideal equal to the product of the determinant of A by all the ideals of I; the determinant of a pseudo-matrix is the determinant of any pseudo-basis of the module it generates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this ideal determinant as the module's 'volume' invariant; computing determinants of pseudo-matrices reduces to det(A) times ∏ a_j (the ideal list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulus in PARI/GP class field theory
rubrics_metrics.description: A modulus (in class field theory) is a divisor supported on the non-complex places of K; in PARI terms this is either an ordinary ideal I (no Archimedean component) or a pair [I, a] where a is a vector with r1 {0,1}-components corresponding to the infinite part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The i-th component of a corresponds to the real embedding attached to the i-th real root of K.roots (ordering depends on chosen defining polynomial). Example: [1,[1,1]] is a modulus for a real quadratic allowing ramification at either infinite place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid (big ideal) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A bid or 'big ideal' is a structure output by idealstar needed to compute in (ZK/I)^*; it is a finite abelian group supplemented by technical data needed to solve discrete log problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bid structures when working with multiplicative groups modulo a modulus; they contain extra data for discrete-log computations and should be accessed via the provided member functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed bnr/bnf input forms for ray class fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Ray number fields (bnr) are defined by a triple A, B, C where [A,B,C] can have forms: [bnr], [bnr, subgroup], [bnr, character], [bnf, mod], [bnf, mod, subgroup]. The last two forms are kept for backward compatibility and no new function will accept them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the modern forms ([bnr], [bnr, subgroup], [bnr, character]). If supplying subgroup, represent it as a square matrix of generators relative to bnr.clgp.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnf and bnr input expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: bnf is as output by bnfinit, where units are mandatory unless the modulus is trivial; bnr is as output by bnrinit. This bnf or bnr is the ground field K for class-field functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using class-field functions, ensure you supply the correctly initialized bnf/bnr structure: bnf must include units unless modulus trivial; many functions require the richer structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup representation for ray class subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: A subgroup of the ray class group modulo f is input as a square matrix expressing generators of a subgroup of bnr.clgp on the given generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing subgroup generators as a matrix allows defining the subfield of the ray class field fixed by that subgroup; this is how you specify congruence subgroups in PARI/GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type hierarchy and argument substitution (nf ≤ bnf ≤ bnr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions specific to relative extensions, number fields, Buchmann’s number fields, Buchmann’s number rays share prefixes rnf, nf, bnf, bnr respectively and take as first argument a number field of that precise type; however it is permissible to use a bnf where a nf is expected (bnf contains more information), while the reverse is not done for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each function requires a minimal type to work; you may substitute a larger type (e.g. pass bnf to an nf-expecting function), but functions that need bnf will not auto-run bnfinit for you (costly) and will error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use member functions rather than direct component access
rubrics_metrics.description: The data types are complicated; never access a component directly, always use a proper member function to retrieve data from structures (once initialized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although components of bnf/bnr are described for completeness, casual users should use member access like bnf.clgp, bnr.bid.no etc., not direct bnf[i] indexing (which is fragile and internal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of bnr/bnf/bid type labels (short list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common member-type labels: bid : bid ideal structure; bnf : Buchmann's number field; clgp : classgroup (with subclasses: cyc=SNF cyclic decomposition, gen=generators); mod : modulus; fu : fundamental units; zk : integral basis; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels are used as suffixes to access structured information: e.g., bnr.bid.no gives φ(f), bnr.bnf.cyc gives class group cyclic decomposition. Consult the manual for full list of members and deprecated entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: P input requirements and nfinit behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: P is the defining polynomial for the number field and must be in Z[X], irreducible and monic. If a non-monic polynomial is supplied, gp issues a warning and transforms it to monic; nfinit returns a vector [res, Mod(a,Q)] giving the change of variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying a non-monic P changes the returned nfinit result (you get the transformation Mod(a,Q)); in other routines the variable change is lost. Prefer supplying monic integer polynomials to avoid surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class group/unit algorithms depend on GRH by default
rubrics_metrics.description: Some bnf* functions implement sub-exponential algorithms for class and unit groups that are correct under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) by default (version ≥ 2.4.0 makes results rigorous under GRH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default, many bnf computations (class number, class group structure, regulators, units) may be wrong if GRH fails; to obtain unconditional correctness use bnfcertify to certify computations. The tech parameter interface is obsolete—do not tamper with it unless you know what you do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of tech vector parameters (c1,c2,nrpid)
rubrics_metrics.description: The obsolete tech vector tech = [c1,c2,nrpid] influences bounds Bi = ci (log |dK|)^2 used to pick factorbases S(Bi); defaults c1 = c2 = 0 (algorithm increases bounds until a GRH proof condition satisfied), Bach gives c2 = 12 as pessimistic uniform bound; nrpid is max number of small-norm relations per ideal (0 disables, reasonable 4..20, default 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users typically should not set tech; the algorithm will increase bounds as needed. If you supply nrpid you must also supply c1,c2 (order matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning about GRH-dependence and bnfcertify
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning: by default most bnf routines depend on GRH; class number, class group structure, class group generators, regulator and fundamental units may be wrong independently. The only guarantee is units generate a subgroup of finite index. Use bnfcertify to certify computations unconditionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run bnfcertify(bnf) after bnfinit if you need unconditional correctness; bnfcertify returns 1 iff the result can be certified without GRH.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfcertify(bnf,{flag=0}) behavior and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfcertify checks whether bnf results are correct without assuming GRH; returns 1 iff correct. It requires the bnf structure to contain the fundamental units unless flag is present (in which case it only certifies that the class group is a quotient and units may be a subgroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bnfcertify complains about missing units, rerun bnfinit with flag=1 to include units (may be expensive). Using bnfcertify(bnf,1) avoids needing units to certify class-group quotient only.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfcompress produces sbnf for compact storage
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfcompress(bnf) computes a compressed 'small Buchmann’s number field' (sbnf) which contains enough information to rapidly recover a full bnf but is much smaller; an sbnf is a 12-component vector with listed components (pol, sign, disc, zk, roots, ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An sbnf is only useful for storage/printing; it must be converted back to a bnf via bnfinit on the sbnf before use. Most nf*/bnf*/bnr* functions do not accept sbnf.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfinit(P,{flag=0},{tech=[]}) semantics and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfinit implements Buchmann's sub-exponential algorithm to compute class group, regulator, and fundamental units for the field defined by irreducible integer polynomial P; by default results are conditional on GRH. flag=1 insists on finding fundamental units exactly (may be very slow or fail if units too large). tech is obsolete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fundamental units are required exactly set flag=1 but be warned about runtime and representation limits; if precision is insufficient units may be omitted by default (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisintnorm and bnfisnorm correctness conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfisintnorm(bnf,x) computes complete systems of solutions (modulo units of positive norm) to Norm(a)=x; if bnf not certified, correctness depends on GRH. bnfisnorm(bnf,x,{flag=1}) tries to tell whether rational x is a norm and returns [a,b] with x = Norm(a)*b; searches for S-unit solutions with S containing primes dividing x and optionally other primes determined by flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bnf is Galois set flag=0 (then x is a norm iff b=1). The answer is guaranteed under GRH if S contains all primes < 12 log(disc(Bnf))^2 (Bnf = Galois closure). Use bnfisintnorm for integer norm problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisprincipal(bnf,x,{flag=1}) output and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether ideal x is principal. Returns [e,t] where e is vector of exponents (0 ≤ e_i < d_i) relative to class-group generators and t a number-field element with x = (t)∏ g_i^{e_i}; x is principal iff e is zero vector. Flags: bit1 toggles whether to output t (0→only e), bit2 warns/instructs on recovering t requiring higher precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use is_principal(bnf,x) = !bnfisprincipal(bnf,x,0) to only test principality. To force recovering t may take long and require increasing precision; prefer symbolic flags nf_GEN and nf_FORCE instead of numeric bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfissunit and bnfisunit behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfissunit(bnf,sfu,x) (with sfu from bnfsunit) returns exponents of x on fundamental S-units and roots of unity; bnfisunit(bnf,x) decomposes unit x on fundamental units and root generator ζ, returning integer exponents [x1,...,xr,xr+1]. If bnf does not contain fundamental units explicitly (due to precision), unit detection still may work but actual unit vectors may be missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fundamental units are absent because bnf was computed with low precision, bnfisunit may still reconstruct exponents (possibly negative) using implicit stored data. To see diagnostics, rerun bnfinit at higher debug/precision levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnflog and logarithmic class-group functions
rubrics_metrics.description: bnflog(bnf,l) returns logarithmic l-class-group invariants [D, G(l), G] where D is elementary divisors for (l)-class group, G(l) elementary divisors for subgroup of logarithmic classes supported at l-adic places, and G some Sylow data; the function returns only if the group is finite (otherwise may loop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions are advanced and conjectural in general (finiteness of logarithmic class group unknown except in some cases). Use only if you understand p-adic/logarithmic class-group theory prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnflogdegree and bnflogef definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: bnflogdegree(nf,A,l) computes the exponential of the l-adic logarithmic degree deg_F A for an ideal A; bnflogef(nf,pr) returns logarithmic ramification and residue degrees [˜e,˜f] for the local extension F_p/Q_p relative to cyclotomic Z_p-extension intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions compute p-adic/logarithmic local invariants; the formulas involve modified e˜ and f˜ defined via intersections with cyclotomic Z_p-extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfnarrow computes narrow class group
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfnarrow(bnf) computes the narrow class group of bnf returning a 3-component row vector v analogous to bnf.clgp: v.no (narrow class number), v.cyc (SNF cyclic components), v.gen (generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a special case of bnrinit; bnf need not contain fundamental units to run bnfnarrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfsignunit, tpuexpo and tpu helpers for totally positive units
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfsignunit(bnf) computes an r1 × (r1 + r2 − 1) ±1 matrix giving signs of real embeddings of fundamental units. tpuexpo(bnf) and tpu(bnf) helper routines compute exponents and generators for totally positive fundamental units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these helper functions to extract a basis of totally positive units in the field; tpuexpo uses linear algebra over Mod(1,2) to compute kernels corresponding to sign constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfsunit computes fundamental S-units and outputs structured vector
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfsunit(bnf,S) computes fundamental S-units where S is a list of prime ideals; output v is a length-6 vector with: v[1] minimal integral generators of S-unit group modulo units, v[2] technical data for bnfissunit, v[3] (deprecated) embeddings, v[4] S-regulator, v[5] S-class group data, v[6] copy of S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call with adequate precision (bnfsunit(GEN bnf, GEN S, long prec)). The returned data is used by bnfissunit and related routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrL1 computes abelian L-values at s=0 or s=1
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrL1(bnr,{H},{flag=0}) returns for each character χ of the ray class group trivial on H the value at s=1 (or s=0) of the abelian L-function attached to χ; for s=0 returns vector [r_χ,c_χ] giving order and first non-zero term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag bits: 1 → compute at s=1 if set (s=0 if unset), 2 → compute primitive L-function vs with Euler factors removed, 3 → return also character. Function may fail with overflow if discriminant too large (too many primes needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrchar constructs characters with prescribed values
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrchar(bnr,g,{v}) returns all characters χ on bnr.clgp such that χ(gi)=e(vi); if v omitted returns characters trivial on gi. g may be a list of ideals or a matrix giving discrete-log coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The vi must be rationals with denominators dividing the order of corresponding generator; using discrete-log matrix encoding allows specifying abstract subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclassno and bnrclassnolist for ray class numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrclassno(A,{B},{C}) returns the relative degree [L:K] for a class field defined by A,B,C (various accepted input types) – in particular ray class numbers; bnrclassnolist(bnf,list) computes many class numbers for a list of moduli (ideallist outputs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnrclassno is faster for a single modulus; bnrclassnolist is useful to enumerate many moduli up to a bound. You may pass a bid structure with generators instead of a full modulus to save time.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrconductor and bnrconductorofchar
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrconductor(A,{B},{C},{flag=0}) returns the conductor f of the subfield defined by [A,B,C]. flag controls whether to return just f (flag=0), [f,Cl_f,H] (flag=1) or [f,bnr(f),H] (flag=2). bnrconductorofchar is obsolete; use bnrconductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may pass a character χ in place of a subgroup H; the routine will return conductor and the character expressed on the minimal ray class group if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisc and bnrdisclist for discriminants
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrdisc(A,{B},{C},{flag=0}) outputs data [N,r1,D] giving discriminant and signature of L depending on flag bits: bit1 controls absolute vs relative data, bit2 returns 0 if modulus not conductor. bnrdisclist(bnf,bound,{arch}) enumerates discriminants of Abelian extensions by increasing modulus norm up to bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnrdisc flag semantics: unset bit1 → absolute data (N=[L:Q]), set → relative data (N=[L:K]). bnrdisclist returns nested vectors encoding moduli and invariants; to decode prime-ideal codings use bnfdecodemodule.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrgaloisapply and bnrgaloismatrix for automorphism action
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrgaloismatrix(bnr,aut) returns the matrix of the action of automorphism aut of base field bnf.nf on the generators bnr.gen; bnrgaloisapply(bnr,mat,H) applies automorphism given by matrix mat to congruence subgroup H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: aut can be given as polynomial, algebraic number, vector of automorphisms, or a Galois group as from galoisinit. When aut is a vector/Galois group, bnrgaloismatrix returns matrices for generators aut.gen.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrinit(bnf,f,{flag=0}) initialization and member access
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrinit initializes data linked to the ray class group for modulus f and returns a bnr structure whose member functions include .bnf (underlying bnf), .mod (modulus), .bid (bid structure), .clgp, .no, .cyc, .gen (ray class group info). If flag=0 (default) generators are not computed (saves time); flag=1 computes generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access class-group data via bnr.clgp, and multiplicative-group data via bnr.bid.*. Do not rely on bnr.gen unless you passed flag=1; computing generators can be time-consuming.
